value.rationale: The invariant is attached to the canonical six-dimensional linear system that realizes the unique unexpected quartic, rather than to an arbitrary slice. Splitting it into the two inequivalent three-dimensional irreducibles explains how the full symmetry acts on every quartic through the configuration and immediately rules out invariant quartics and low-dimensional invariant subsystems. This is a natural structural datum for symmetry-reduced interpolation and for comparisons with other root-system unexpected configurations.
